 Live Now Dallas weather: Storms move across North Texas overnight before 2026 elections
 By Ali Turiano  and  Dan Henry Weather Published  November 2, 2026 5:38 AM CST Published  November 2, 2026 5:38 AM CST The Brief
 A strong cold front bringing severe storms will sweep through North Texas overnight. 
 The primary threat is damaging wind gusts up to 60 mph, which can cause damage similar to a weak tornado. 
 A Tornado Watch is in effect in some north-west North Texas counties until 11 p.m. on Monday, and more storms could move through the metroplex overnight. 
 DALLAS - A weather system that caused historic flooding across the Southwest is heading toward North Texas. 
 Live Updates
 9:50 p.m.: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued for several counties
 9 p.m.: Timeline for November 2 storms
 A Tornado Watch remains in effect for western and northwestern counties in North Texas.
 Storms and severe weather in those areas is expected to end around 11 p.m., when the Tornado Watch is scheduled to expire.
 For the I-35 corridor of North Texas, the storms could move into Tarrant and Denton counties by 10 p.m., and are expected to move through Dallas County overnight.
 Eastern parts of the FOX 4 viewing area can expect the storms to pass through from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. 
 6:50 p.m.: Tornado Watch issued for multiple North Texas counties
 A Tornado Watch is currently in effect for Hood County, Palo Pinto County, Parker County, Comanche County, Jack County, Wise County, Cooke County, and Erath County.
 The watch was issued at 5:50 p.m. and is in effect until 11 p.m.
 Nov. 2 overnight forecast
 Dallas weather: November 2 overnight forecast 
 Severe weather is moving across North Texas overnight. FOX 4's chief meteorologist Dan Henry has more on when it'll hit where you live in this overnight forecast for November 2.
 Send Us Your Photos!
 Severe Weather Risk and Timing
 What we know:
 Storms will begin developing to the north and west between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. this evening. The system will move closer to the I-35 corridor by 10 p.m.
 The primary threat is damaging wind gusts up to 60 mph, which can cause damage similar to a weak tornado.
 Large hail, up to the size of quarters, and localized flooding are also possible.
 Temperatures will drop from a high of 85 degrees today to about 73 degrees behind the cold front.
 Local perspective:
 The rain is expected to move out of the immediate Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex by the early morning commute at 4 a.m. 
 Voters in eastern and southeastern counties, stretching into East Texas, may still see rain when polls open around 7 a.m. 
 Voters in eastern areas might consider waiting until the afternoon to cast their ballots, as the region will dry out quickly once the front passes.
 What's next:
 Following the storms, strong north-west winds up to 25 mph will dry out the area quickly. 
 The rest of the week will have seasonal, comfortable conditions with highs in the 70s. 
 The region will remain mostly rain-free, aside from a low rain chance along the Red River on Thursday.
 7-day Forecast 
 The Source: The information in this article comes from FOX 4's Ali Turiano.
